label: Politik
_comment_feeds: Bill-linked coverage plus straight political reporting. The wider set exists because the sphere now has two paths: a bill on Congress.gov when the coverage names one, and political news or circulating claims when it does not. Without the second path a week with no floor action produced an empty episode, which is what kept happening.
_comment_scoring: Deterministic. The model never scores. Each rule is a plain fact read off the Congress.gov response.
_comment_cap: Hard ceiling. If only one item clears the threshold the episode has one item. If none clear it, the episode says so and the sphere yields its slot.
_comment_script: Rules handed to the model verbatim when it writes the podcast script.
scriptRules: När ett lagförslag finns: dokumentet är ämnet, och bevakningen är kontexten. Aldrig tvärtom.
När inget lagförslag finns: säg rakt ut att avsnittet bygger på bevakning, inte på primärkällor.
Ett obekräftat påstående beskrivs som att det cirkulerar, med vem som rapporterar det. Aldrig som ett faktum, och aldrig som enda grund för ett stycke.
Attribuera varje orsakssamband till den som hävdar det.
Förklara amerikansk process bara när den är verkligt obskyr. Karl vet vad ett utskott är.
_comment_fallback: What happens when no coverage links to a bill. The primary path is unchanged and still preferred: a bill on Congress.gov is a document, and a document beats reporting about a document. This only runs when that path returns nothing, and it says so in the script rather than passing teasers off as primary-source work.
_comment_rumours: The same three tiers val2026 uses, and the same rule. Washington runs on anonymous sourcing, so excluding unconfirmed claims would exclude half of what actually moves - but a circulating claim is described AS circulation, never restated as fact, and never carries an item on its own.
